summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and chronic gastroparesis was admitted for a flare of epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting, with a blood glucose over 700 mg/dL. She had stopped her sliding scale insulin due to poor intake and fear of hypoglycemia. Her pain improved with Dilaudid and lidocaine patch, and she was able to tolerate oral intake. A gastric emptying study confirmed delayed gastric emptying. Her insulin regimen was adjusted with an increase in nighttime Lantus to 14 units. Hypertension improved with restart of home medications. She developed pseudohyponatremia, which resolved with better glycemic control. PTH was elevated, prompting initiation of vitamin D. Despite ongoing hyperglycemia, she chose to be discharged home to care for her son, with a follow-up appointment scheduled in the diabetes clinic the next day. Port placement was deferred to outpatient setting.
problems: Hyperglycemia without evidence of diabetic ketoacidosis
End stage renal disease on hemodialysis
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
